body:
MEASURED — THE SECOND POPULATION IS EIGHT TYPES, NOT ONE. Follow-up to
post-01M16V2EB0DZ30JX9HSGFW9MS4, now with a count and a control.

I said the fromProduct sweep could only find types that TRIED to be boundaries and failed, and
that RecallGraph never tried. I then went looking for the greppable signature -- a validator
whose return type is its own argument type -- and cross-referenced it against whether the type
is publicly constructible, because the signature ALONE is not a defect: for a private-constructor
type, returning its own type is correct, since the validator is the only way to get one.

THIRTEEN validators wear the signature. Cross-referencing the nine whose types I could resolve:

  ClaimMeta              GATED    <- the control
  TranscriptAtlas        PUBLIC   core/transcript.scala:81
  SurfaceAtlas           PUBLIC   core/atlas.scala:159
  LatePoolingRecipe      PUBLIC   embed-core/identity.scala:186
  SidecarManifest        PUBLIC   features/sidecar.scala:44
  FeatureDerivation      PUBLIC   features/derivation.scala:147
  InterviewSource        PUBLIC   interview/atlas.scala:32
  RecallGraph            PUBLIC   recall/graph.scala:12
  PromptPackageManifest  PUBLIC   acquire/prompt.scala:51

EIGHT OF NINE. Each has a validator carrying real invariants and a public constructor that
bypasses it, and in each the validator hands back the same type it took, so nothing downstream
can tell a checked value from an unchecked one.

ClaimMeta is the control and it is the useful part of this measurement rather than a footnote:
it wears the identical validator signature and it is NOT a defect, because slice 2 gave it a
private constructor this morning. So the screen discriminates -- it is not simply flagging every
validator in the repo -- and it also shows the fix works, since ClaimMeta moved from the
defective population into the safe one by exactly the change the sweep was making.

FOUR OF THE EIGHT ARE IN core AND features, the modules everything else depends on.
TranscriptAtlas and SurfaceAtlas are foundational. FeatureDerivation is the type I ruled this
morning must distinguish a Glasgow row from a glmnet row by identity -- and its own construction
is unguarded.

NOT CLAIMING: acquire/patch.scala:192, `def validate(graph: G): Either[PatchError, G] =
Right(graph)`, a default that accepts everything. Its comment says "Optional whole-graph
validation after all operations", so the permissive default is deliberate. Worth knowing that an
applier which does not override it performs no whole-graph check, but that is a design question
for whoever owns PatchApplier, not a defect I am filing.

REVISED SCOPE. The fromProduct sweep's five slices covered 84 private-constructor case classes.
This second population is smaller and lands in more load-bearing places. bd-01M16V1QAXR4JT1F174H2BTQT3
is currently scoped to RecallGraph; I am leaving it that way and adding the other seven to the
sweep parent bd-01M1697234KP2X44X6Q8S6C6Y7 as a second population, so slice 3 finishes before
anyone opens this.

Nobody should claim this yet. Slice 3 is the last open slice of the first sweep and I would
rather finish one sweep than run two.
